column1: Question stem says ALWAYS / NEVER / MUST / deterministic. Which kind of answer wins?
column2:
A mechanism that makes the wrong action impossible: hook, code gate, schema, tool_choice, remove the tool.
Trap: "add it to the prompt" (probabilistic).

column1: Question is about varied, ambiguous, or inconsistent output (no hard rule). Which kind of answer wins?
column2:
The lightest fix at the root cause: clearer tool descriptions, explicit criteria, few-shot examples.
Trap: bigger model, new infrastructure.

column1: Agent skips a required step (e.g. verify identity before refund) in 8% of cases. Fix?
column2:
Programmatic prerequisite gate: the refund tool rejects unless verification succeeded.
Trap: stronger prompt or few-shot (lowers rate, never 0).

column1: Router agent has route_ticket + process_refund "just in case" and misuses refund. Fix?
column2:
Remove the extra tools. Give each agent only the tools its role needs.
Trap: "NEVER call refund" in the prompt.

column1: Data formats vary (dates, prices). Conversion must be deterministic + unit-testable. Design?
column2:
Claude extracts the raw string; application code converts.
Trap: schema pattern or format: "date" (validates shape, Claude still converts).

column1: Extraction from wildly varied layouts invents values; detailed rules did not help. Next step?
column2: Few-shot examples of diverse layouts, incl. one where the field is absent → null. Make fields nullable.

column1: tool_choice: Claude must call some tool every turn, and picks which.
column2: {"type": "any"}

column1: tool_choice: Claude must call one specific tool every time.
column2: {"type": "tool", "name": "..."}

column1: tool_choice: default; Claude may answer without a tool.
column2: {"type": "auto"}

column1: Which tool_choice values work with manual extended thinking?
column2: Only auto and none. any/tool give an error.

column1: PreToolUse hook returns permissionDecision "deny" + reason. Effect?
column2: Tool call is blocked. The reason is shown to Claude, so it can adapt (e.g. use the safe wrapper).

column1: PreToolUse permissionDecision "allow" vs "ask": who sees the reason?
column2: The user. allow = runs, skips the prompt. ask = user confirms.

column1: Can a PostToolUse hook stop a dangerous call?
column2: No. It runs after the tool already ran. Use PreToolUse to block. PostToolUse is for normalizing/checking results.

column1: Agents must message each other directly and share a task list over a long session. Pattern?
column2:
Agent teams (experimental flag).
Subagents only return a final result to their caller.

column1: Can a Claude Code subagent start other subagents?
column2: No. Hub-and-spoke: the coordinator starts subagents.

column1: Foreground subagent writes text, then an API error cuts it off. What does the coordinator get?
column2:
The partial text + a note that it was cut off. (Claude Code first prompts it to continue.)
No text at all → "Agent terminated early due to an API error".

column1: How does a subagent get the context it needs?
column2: Explicitly in its prompt. It does not see the coordinator's conversation.

column1: Agentic loop: which stop_reason means "run the tool and continue"? Which means "done"?
column2:
tool_use → run the tool, send result, loop.
end_turn → stop.

column1: Config for: only me, this repo, never in git.
column2: CLAUDE.local.md in repo root (add it to .gitignore).

column1: Config for: team, this repo, in git.
column2: ./CLAUDE.md (or .claude/CLAUDE.md). Also what CI runs load.

column1: Config for: only me, every repo.
column2: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md

column1: Conventions that apply only to some files (e.g. tests spread across folders).
column2:
.claude/rules/*.md with paths: glob frontmatter.
Trap: root CLAUDE.md (always loads).

column1: Team-shared slash command for this repo.
column2: .claude/commands/ (committed). Personal: ~/.claude/commands/.

column1: MCP server shared with everyone who clones the repo.
column2: .mcp.json in repo root. Personal: ~/.claude.json.

column1: CI must apply team review rules on every run without editing each workflow. Where?
column2: The repo's committed CLAUDE.md. CI runners have no personal ~/.claude.

column1: Run Claude Code non-interactively in CI with machine-readable output.
column2: claude -p "..." --output-format json (add --json-schema for a fixed shape).

column1: Plan mode vs direct execution?
column2: Plan mode: large/multi-file or unclear change. Direct: small, well-defined change.

column1: MCP tool fails. How should it report the error?
column2: Structured error: isError: true + category + retryable. Never hide it; never end the whole workflow.

column1: Escalate to a human based on the model's self-reported confidence or customer sentiment?
column2: No, unreliable signals. Use explicit escalation criteria.

column1: When is the Message Batches API the right answer?
column2: Only for non-blocking work (50% cheaper, up to 24 h). Never when a user is waiting.

column1: Reviewing a large multi-file change for bugs. Best approach?
column2:
Per-file passes + a separate cross-file integration pass.
Trap: bigger model, majority vote.
